title: Chronicle resumption engine with observed-state pruning for analytics re-ingest
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: When we run long-running re-ingests or backfills for console usage analytics, we repeatedly reapply already-materialized aggregates and user events because our replay jobs ingest from event storage without a lightweight observed-state checkpoint. This increases CPU/GPU cost in downstream transforms and causes transient duplicate counts in dashboards and alerts.

Goal: Build a resumption engine (Chronicle) that can restart replay/backfill jobs using compact observed-state pruning to skip ranges already applied, produce an idempotent replay stream, and expose resumable checkpoints for operator tooling.

Success metrics: (1) End-to-end cost for large replays reduced by 40% on average for typical runs (>1B events). (2) Mean time to resume after failure < 5 minutes. (3) Dashboard diffs between baseline and replayed aggregates within 0.1% for weekly retention tests.

Scope and constraints: Console analytics pipelines are heterogeneous (Realtime, Batch, Feature extraction). Chronicle will target the secondary re-ingest path used by oss-analytics and console-metrics for the first iteration. Must be backwards-compatible with existing ingest schemas and must not require a global coordination service beyond a lightweight coordinator (etcd-backed).

Design overview:
- Snapshot-driven checkpoints: periodic compact checkpoints (protobuf) emitted by the projection layer that record high-water marks and materialized keys with TTL.
- Observed-state pruning: when a replay job resumes, it consults the checkpoint to prune contiguous ranges of events whose materialized state matches the checkpoint and then streams only the deltas.
- Idempotent apply layer: introduce deterministic apply tokens for each event window to guarantee safe replays without double-counting.
- Safety fences: a dry-run mode that computes diffs against a canary dataset and an approval gate before a replay can update production aggregates.

Artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Chronicle+Resumption+Engine
- Architecture diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ChronicleArch
- Specification proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-protos/pull/128
- Initial operator UI mock: https://figma.com/redwood/chronicle-ops

Rollout plan: prototype in staging using a small dataset (100M events) -> run end-to-end against console-metrics -> iterate on checkpoint cadence and pruning heuristics -> enable dry-run for production replays -> GA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Resume from checkpoint skips >=90% of materialized keys in controlled replay tests. 2) Deterministic tokens prevent visible duplicate aggregates in 10/10 replay runs. 3) Operator can trigger dry-run and see candidate diffs in Console UI. 4) Metrics for resume latency and skipped event ratio emitted to telemetry. 5) Integration tests added to analytics-replay CI with flakiness <1%.
implementation_notes:
Prototype uses RocksDB-backed compact checkpoint store with protobuf snapshots; coordinator service exposes gRPC resume/checkpoint APIs. We'll add a compatibility flag in the ingest layer to read deterministic apply tokens and opt into pruning. Performance-critical pruning logic will be implemented in Rust (via analytics-runtime crate) and surfaced to existing Go runners via FFI.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Strong global coordination would simplify correctness but increase operational blast radius; chosen lightweight checkpointing reduces coordination cost at the expense of slightly more complex pruning heuristics. 2) More frequent checkpoints reduce replay cost but increase normal ingest latency; default cadence set to 15 minutes with config per pipeline.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Maya: Kicked off PRD review with Console PMs. Main ask: ensure the operator flow doesn't require deep infra expertise. Added operator mock links.

2026-02-18 - Rafael: Spike implemented snapshot format and local pruning simulation. Found that naive key-list checkpoints exceed 20GB for the largest customer; switched to Bloom-filter + range-hash summarization for practical sizing.
2026-02-25 - Design review (Leah): Suggested adding a visual diff step in Console to preview replay effects before commit; added a dry-run acceptance criterion.
2026-03-03 - Infra review (Anika): Flagged need for GC of checkpoints and retention policy; created follow-up ENG-60219 to add retention TTL to checkpointstore.
2026-03-08 - Rafael: Opened proto PR for checkpoint spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-protos/pull/128 - feedback requested from infra and runtime teams.
2026-03-10 - Maya: Ran end-to-end staging run with 120M events, resume skipped 62% of events after pruning on first pass; performance looks promising but hotspotting observed on a single shard.
2026-03-12 - Rafael: Mitigation for shard hotspotting added: adaptive checkpoint cadence and shard-aware pruning. Marking as In Progress and scheduling implementation work for Cycle 2026-W10.
